- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.3), increase downward bias or add early mean-reversion correction.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast growth to 3–4% per day.  
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days falling from 80+), reduce forecast slope and add 1–2 day lagged correction.  
- If forecast is rising steadily but true outcome shows early divergence (e.g., 3–5 days of underperformance), reduce forecast by 1–2% per day starting from day 5.  
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend (all 0.00), forecast should be anchored to recent 7–14 day moving average, not extrapolated.
